claim_boundary: This memory-task-transit contract, its host-receipt schema and its synthetic receipts are a schema-level alignment artifact only. No live cutover, no BACH runtime change, no working-memory write, no BACH-IN, no migration, no rollback, and no parity acceptance is performed or implied.

hold.rule: Do not modify, push, boot, or wire BACH working memory into a live transit during the active hold. Receipts are static, synthetic and temporary; the checker validates shape and reconciliation only.

claim_signal.description: A host participates in the memory-task transit by emitting a signed receipt that binds its host_id to the shared task_uid, stable_id and contents. The receipt signature is a SHA-256 over the ordered canonical receipt fields plus the claim salt; the salt itself is never published in clear.

reconciliation.description: All three host receipts must agree on task_uid, stable_id, transit_scope, privacy_class, logical_task_id and payload_digest. Any divergence is a reconciliation failure.

double_claim_prohibition.description: A host_id may appear in exactly one receipt per stable_id. Sequences must be unique across all receipts for the same stable_id. A host may not claim the same transit row twice.

memory_task_transit.description: Transport of a single BACH working-memory pointer row across three anonymized hosts.
memory_task_transit.notes: Receipts are synthetic fingerprints; they do not prove real host possession.

next_gates: Keep tools/check_memory_task_transit.py as a required regression gate and stop on receipt schema or host-set drift.
Keep the memory-task-transit contract free of any live cutover, runtime wiring, migration, or parity acceptance until explicit review.
After the hold, run one anonymized real working-memory row through the same schema and compare receipts.
Only then design BACH-IN memory-transit adapters and rollback guards.
Keep the claim salt exclusively with LEAD TRITHON; any additional claim authority is a separate reviewed change.
